entries.subject: ISAM SAGE 102: selected nonconvex shape
entries.finding: The actual recipe selects shape/isam-sage-102.obj, not DAMIT 1869 named in the older comparison metadata. The retained original OBJ header identifies target 159, SAGE, 3842 vertices, 7680 facets, pole (138.85848°, 65.93886°) and period 24.478724 h. These match the rounded SAGE pole-1 solution in Marciniak 2018 Table 3; the recipe applies its separately documented 135 km volume scale.

entries.subject: Registered surface imagery
entries.finding: The grid marks unavailable imagery; rotation phase is illustrative.
entries.revisitWhen: A released, reusable surface observation or mapped product with registration to this body’s selected source model; the existing grid alone does not imply that every archive was searched.

entries.subject: Shape and spin alternatives
entries.finding: SAGE pole 2 remains a viable alternative, with a different published occultation scale. The actual source header matches pole 1, so neither the alternate pole scale nor the older convex model scale belongs on this mesh without a new fit.
entries.revisitWhen: A released numerical replacement or independent pole/size constraints that distinguish the recorded alternatives, followed by comparison against the currently selected model.

entries.subject: ISAM models: included original SAGE102; companion101 is the mirror pole
entries.finding: - [ISAM models](http://isam.astro.amu.edu.pl/home2.php?obiekt=159&lang=en&strona=1&typ=Interactive%20mode&nr_modelu=1): included original SAGE102; companion101 is the mirror pole. HTTP works; HTTPS failed TLS. The linked metadata page is empty, so the original OBJ header and publication own the method and calibration claims.

entries.subject: Marciniak 2018: SAGE pole-1 calibration
entries.finding: Tables 3 and 4 were checked against the OBJ header and recipe. The occultation-calibrated SAGE pole-1 diameter is 135 ±7 km; pole 2 is 138 ±7 km, while the convex solutions are 130 km. The four-chord 2009 occultation does not uniquely select a pole. Section 5.1 gives a marginal thermophysical preference for SAGE pole 1 with 137 ±8 km. The selected calibration remains supported without treating this inverse model as photographed terrain.

entries.subject: DAMIT convex 1869: excluded from the displayed source, retained as comparison
entries.finding: - [DAMIT convex 1869](https://damit.cuni.cz/projects/damit/asteroid_models/view/1869): excluded from the displayed source, retained as comparison. Its archive 140±7 km and the paper's convex 130±7 km refer to different reported scales; neither is substituted into SAGE geometry.
entries.revisitWhen: A changed source release adds independently useful geometry or metadata beyond the selected model; compare it before changing the displayed source.

entries.subject: AKARI AcuA v1.0 is retained only for comparison
entries.finding: - AKARI AcuA v1.0 is retained only for comparison. A thermal effective-sphere diameter is not used when the source-supported occultation calibration exists.
entries.revisitWhen: Published model-specific definitions, an independently constrained pole/scale, or a released replacement mesh that resolves the recorded ambiguity.

entries.subject: Marciniak et al
entries.finding: - [Marciniak et al. (2018), Photometric survey, modelling, and scaling of long-period and low-amplitude asteroids](https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018A%26A...610A...7M) — selected model publication.
